children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're asking about your son Alex, who is 13 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, this affects eligibility, but there are some circumstances where you may still be able to claim Child Benefit.

**Can you tell me which country you're currently living in, and are you or your partner a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted abroad)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad, but I'm not a Crown servant - I don't work for the diplomatic service or armed forces or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. 

To determine your eligibility while living abroad, I need to know a bit more about your specific situation:

**Which country are you currently living in?** (This is important because you may be able to get Child Benefit if you live in certain countries, particularly some EEA countries or Switzerland, depending on your circumstances.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not say exactly which country - does it really matter for whether I can claim?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand your concern about privacy. However, yes, the specific country does matter significantly for Child Benefit eligibility.

According to the rules, you may be able to get Child Benefit if you "go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant." Since you've confirmed you're not a Crown servant, eligibility depends on whether you're living in one of those "certain countries" - which typically refers to specific arrangements with EEA countries or Switzerland.

Without knowing which country you're in, I cannot definitively determine whether you qualify under the rules for claiming Child Benefit while living abroad. The eligibility criteria are different depending on your country of residence.

**Are you able to tell me if you're living in an EEA (European Economic Area) country or Switzerland?** Even this general information would help me assess your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. Well, I'm not in an EEA country or Switzerland - it's somewhere else entirely.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is important information.

Based on what you've told me:
- You're living abroad (outside the UK)
- You're not in an EEA country or Switzerland
- You're not a Crown servant

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 **and you live in the UK**. The rules state you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries (typically EEA/Switzerland) or if you're a Crown servant.

Since you don't fall into either of these exceptions and you're not living in the UK, this means you would not be eligible for UK Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me make my assessment:

## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible** for UK Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

While Alex meets the age requirement at 13 years old (under 16), the main issue is that you don't currently live in the UK. The general rule for Child Benefit is that you must be responsible for a child under 16 **and live in the UK**.

There are only limited exceptions for people living abroad:
- Those living in certain countries (typically EEA countries or Switzerland)
- Crown servants (diplomats, armed forces personnel, etc.)

Since you're living outside the UK in a country that's not in the EEA or Switzerland, and you're not a Crown servant, you don't meet the residency requirement for claiming UK Child Benefit.

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you return to live in the UK), you could potentially claim Child Benefit at that time.
